prompt.context: Our client is PLD, a global manufacturer of snack foods and beverages. PLD has been a market leader in China's potato chips (PC) market for over two decades but is facing increasing local competition. Most notably this year, the company's volume share in the South China region declined from 60% to 20%, and the company hired us to find out why and how to react.
prompt.question: Why did PLD's volume share in South China decline from 60% to 20%, and how should PLD react?

clarifying_info.q: What do we know about PLD's products?
clarifying_info.a: Consumers see current potato chips products as commodities, so average price is similar across competition. Currently all potato chips are fried but PLD is considering introducing baked products which use minimal or no oil in production.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the consumers in the potato chips market?
clarifying_info.a: There are two primary consumer groups: the Totally Fried Guys (TFGs) who prefer the crispness of current fried products, and the Completely Baked Dudes (CBDs) who prefer baked products with less or no oil. TFGs comprise 80% of total market consumption but more people are switching to the CBD group. Assume no seasonality in consumption.

clarifying_info.q: What are the national market figures for PLD and competitors?
clarifying_info.a: Last year, PLD recorded 800,000 tons of sales in the national PC market with 40% market share, followed by WWT (10%) and DLT (5%).

clarifying_info.q: What are the South China regional figures?
clarifying_info.a: The South China Region accounts for 10% of the overall national PC market. Last year PLD sold 120,000 tons of PC in South China with 60% market share; the rest of the market goes to WWT (20%) and DLT (20%).

clarifying_info.q: What is PLD's current year volume in South China?
clarifying_info.a: PLD's volume is 132,000 tons at the close of this year.

clarifying_info.q: What happened with WWT and DLT volumes this year?
clarifying_info.a: WWT and DLT volumes grew by 10% this year.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a new competitor in the market?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, there was one new competitor, XCD, which entered the South China market in the middle of this year. XCD has been in the market for only 3 months (it is now September) and generated 280,000 tons of sales.

clarifying_info.q: Why is XCD doing so well?
clarifying_info.a: The key is product — XCD introduced a baked product. It was the CBD group buying the newly launched baked product.

clarifying_info.q: Where did the new CBD consumers come from?
clarifying_info.a: Most of them were NOT switchers from the TFG group. The majority of CBD consumers this year were previous non-consumers of potato chips — people concerned about oil in fried products who are now entering the category to buy XCD's baked product.

clarifying_info.q: Has the frequency of eating potato chips changed?
clarifying_info.a: No, frequency of eating potato chips has not changed for either group.

framework: Snack Competition: flavor trends, health trends, pricing changes, distribution channel changes
Snacker Market: total market growth, segment growth, changes in taste, changes in chip type
PLD's Business: discontinued chip flavors, new pricing strategy, supply chain changes, lawsuits, public relations scandals

questions.prompt: PLD's volume in South China is 132,000 tons this year vs. 120,000 tons last year. What does this tell us?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize this represents 10% volume growth for PLD year-over-year. PLD is not shrinking — it is growing. This is important because the share decline (60% to 20%) is NOT caused by a volume decline on PLD's part.

math.setup: Compare this year's volume (132,000) to last year's volume (120,000).
math.answer: PLD grew 10% in South China this year.

questions.prompt: Given PLD now holds 20% market share with 132,000 tons, what is the total South China market size this year? How does that compare to last year?
questions.guidance: Candidate must infer total market size from PLD's volume and new market share, then compare to last year's 200,000 tons. The huge market size jump is the key insight: the share loss is driven by market expansion, not by PLD losing existing customers.

math.setup: If PLD = 132,000 tons = 20% share, then total market = 132,000 / 0.20.
steps: Last year total South China market = 200,000 tons
math.answer: The South China market grew from 200,000 to 660,000 tons — a 230% jump. PLD's share loss is due to explosive market growth, not volume decline.

questions.prompt: WWT and DLT also grew 10%. What does this tell us about the source of market growth?
questions.guidance: If all three incumbents grew only 10%, they are not the source of the massive market expansion. New entrant(s) must account for the difference. Candidate should calculate the combined incumbent volume and identify the gap.

math.setup: Apply 10% growth to last year's WWT and DLT South China volumes, sum with PLD's current volume, and compare to total market.
math.answer: Incumbents together account for only 220,000 of 660,000 tons. A new competitor accounts for roughly 440,000 tons and about 67% of the market.

questions.prompt: Probe on the new competitor XCD: quantify its performance and explain why it is doing so well (use 4Ps).
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify XCD entered only 3 months ago and quantify its monthly run rate vs. PLD's. On 4Ps, the key differentiator is Product — XCD launched a baked chip targeting the CBD consumer segment, which attracted a wave of previous non-consumers who avoided fried products.

math.setup: Calculate XCD monthly volume vs. PLD monthly volume.
steps: XCD monthly volume is 93,333 / 11,000 = ~8.5x PLD's monthly volume
math.answer: XCD's monthly volume is more than 8 times PLD's despite being in the market only 3 months.

questions.prompt: The CBD group was only 20% of market volume last year but is now more than half. Where did these new CBD consumers come from?
questions.guidance: Candidate should reason that frequency has not changed for either group. Therefore the growth cannot come from TFG-to-CBD switching alone (that would simply reallocate existing volume). Most new CBD consumers must be previous non-consumers who are now entering the category because a non-oily baked alternative exists. This is a market-expansion story, not a share-steal story.

math.setup: XCD monthly ~93K vs. rest of market monthly ~55K (220K/12 * 3 months condensed view).
steps: CBD share of current monthly volume = 93,000 / (93,000 + 55,000) = 93,000 / 148,000 = ~63%
Last year CBD = 20% of 200,000 = 40,000 tons; now CBD = ~440,000 tons (new entrant volume)
The jump far exceeds what switching from TFG could explain
math.answer: The majority of CBD consumers are new entrants to the category, not switchers from TFG, indicating baked chips expanded the total market rather than cannibalizing fried chips.

brainstorming.prompt: How should PLD react to the competitive threat from XCD?

categories.name: Short-term defense of fried segment
ideas: Increase marketing investment targeting TFG consumers
Launch promotional pricing or bundles in South China
Introduce new flavors or limited-edition products to excite TFG group
Increase shelf space or distribution coverage in South China retail
Partner with key retailers for exclusive placement or end-cap displays

categories.name: Long-term product innovation
ideas: Develop and launch PLD's own baked potato chip product targeting CBD consumers
Accelerate R&D on low-oil or no-oil chip technology
Test baked product in South China before national rollout
Build baked product as a separate brand or sub-brand to avoid cannibalizing fried line

categories.name: Competitive response — M&A
ideas: Consider acquiring XCD before it scales nationally
Acquire XCD's baked product technology or production capabilities

categories.name: Market monitoring and intelligence
ideas: Track whether CBD trend spreads from South China to other regions
Conduct consumer research to size the CBD opportunity nationally
Assess supply chain cost of baked vs. fried production

recommendation: In the short term, XCD's growth is expanding the total market rather than stealing directly from PLD's existing customers, and XCD operates only in South China (10% of national volume). The immediate threat to PLD's core TFG business is limited.

In the long term, the CBD trend and XCD's exceptional performance in South China suggest XCD is likely to expand nationally. PLD must proactively develop or acquire a baked chip capability before XCD replicates its South China success at national scale.
risks: XCD may accelerate national rollout before PLD can launch a competing baked product
If the CBD trend accelerates, TFG volume could decline as consumers shift preferences
PLD's baked product could cannibalize its own fried chip sales
Acquisition of XCD may be expensive given its rapid growth trajectory
next_steps: Immediately launch a baked chip R&D program or evaluate acquisition of XCD
Protect South China market share with targeted marketing and promotions for TFG consumers
Conduct national consumer research to forecast the CBD segment growth trajectory
Develop a staged rollout plan for a baked product line with South China as the first market
